sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: *Te* is one friend: *tanulsz*. To speak to two or more friends, say *ti* (“you all”) and add *-tok*, *-tek* or *-tök* to the stem. The vowels choose, as they do for “I”: back vowels *-tok*, front vowels *e* and *é* *-tek*, and *ö, ő, ü, ű* *-tök*. In a mixed stem such as *sétál* the last vowel decides: *sétáltok*.

sections.title: Which ending?
sections.content: *Olvas* becomes *olvastok*, *tanul* becomes *tanultok*. *Beszél* becomes *beszéltek*, *kérdez* becomes *kérdeztek*. *Főz* becomes *főztök*. No linking vowel is needed, even when the stem ends in *s* or *z*: *olvas* + *tok* is *olvastok*, while the single “you” is *olvasol*.

items.english: In the afternoon you all walk in the park.
Do you all have lunch here at noon?

sections.content: *Ír* is neutral, like *írok*: *írtok*. Say *tanulsz?* to one friend and *tanultok?* to a group.
